editorial_intro: Suriya's blockbuster Karuppu finally hits streaming, Akshay Kumar's spooky comeback Bhooth Bangla arrives on Netflix, and Ali Fazal anchors a gripping true-crime thriller in Raakh — plus Dhurandhar 2 is still dominating JioHotstar.

picks.title: Karuppu
picks.synopsis: Tamil fantasy actioner where Suriya plays Lord Vettai Karuppu, who descends to Earth in human form as a lawyer to fight systemic corruption and deliver justice to an exploited family. RJ Balaji directs and co-stars as the corrupt antagonist.
picks.why_watch: Suriya in god mode — literally. The year's biggest Tamil blockbuster finally hits streaming.

picks.title: Bhooth Bangla
picks.synopsis: A man inherits a palace in rural Mangalpur and plans his sister's wedding there, but strange supernatural events and panicked locals force him to investigate the property's mysterious past. Akshay Kumar reunites with director Priyadarshan for this horror-comedy romp.
picks.why_watch: The Akshay-Priyadarshan reunion we've been waiting for. Hera Pheri energy meets horror comedy.

picks.title: Raakh
picks.synopsis: Set in 1978 Delhi, this investigative crime thriller follows Sub-Inspector Jayprakash during a relentless manhunt after the mysterious disappearance of two teenagers. Inspired by the real-life Geeta and Sanjay Chopra abduction case, the psychological drama explores human depravity and the toll of guilt.
picks.why_watch: Ali Fazal in a gritty 70s period thriller inspired by a real case — dark, intense, and beautifully shot.

picks.title: Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge
picks.synopsis: Undercover agent Jaskirat Singh Rangi rises through the ranks of the Karachi underworld to become Sher-e-Baloch. He must eliminate rival threats and dismantle terror funding while evading the ISI. The sequel that crossed ₹1,100 Cr in theaters is now streaming.
picks.why_watch: The ₹1,100 crore blockbuster — the biggest Hindi film of the year — is finally on your screen at home.

picks.title: Gullak Season 5
picks.synopsis: The Mishra family returns with elder son Annu facing career pressures and apartment hunting, while younger Aman comes back from college more mature. Matriarch Shanti gains an online identity and Santosh introduces modern home updates — wholesome middle-class storytelling at its finest.
picks.why_watch: If you grew up in a middle-class Indian household, Gullak hits different. Season 5 doesn't disappoint.

picks.title: Dridam
picks.synopsis: A young police officer begins his first posting in a quiet town, but the calm quickly breaks when serious crimes erupt. As he investigates, he uncovers hidden corruption and shifting loyalties that force him to confront both the case and his own understanding of justice.
picks.why_watch: Malayalam cinema keeps delivering — a slow-burn crime thriller with Shane Nigam in top form.

picks.title: I Will Find You
picks.synopsis: David Burroughs is serving a life sentence for his son's murder. When evidence emerges suggesting the child may still be alive, he escapes prison and embarks on a dangerous search for the truth, uncovering shocking secrets. Based on the bestselling Harlan Coben novel.
picks.why_watch: Harlan Coben adaptation on Netflix — if you liked The Stranger or Fool Me Once, this is your next binge.

picks.title: Shelter
picks.synopsis: A reclusive former government assassin's forced isolation is shattered when a stranded supply girl triggers a lethal tracking system, forcing him to defend her against his old handler's relentless execution squads. Jason Statham does what Jason Statham does best.
picks.why_watch: Statham + Bill Nighy + remote wilderness = popcorn-grade action therapy for your weekend.

picks.title: Michael
picks.synopsis: The early life of Michael Jackson, from the discovery of his talent as the lead of the Jackson Five to his relentless pursuit to become the biggest entertainer in the world. Jaafar Jackson (Michael's nephew) stars in the title role.
picks.why_watch: MJ's nephew playing MJ, directed by Antoine Fuqua — the most anticipated music biopic in years.

picks.title: Your Fault: London
picks.synopsis: When Noah and Nick's relationship faces fresh challenges — old wounds, family tensions and lingering doubts threaten to pull them apart. As they navigate love, trust and personal ambitions, both must decide whether their bond is strong enough to survive.
picks.why_watch: The Culpa franchise goes to London — perfect guilty-pleasure romance for a lazy weekend.
